active_problem.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and "fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills."
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from a ~600/month baseline (610, 590) to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09) (E-07).
Majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) occur on bills carrying ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02).

active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07) because, per the only surviving supported hypothesis (H-RULE-CHANGE), a change to billing import validation rules around August causes the billing system to compute or accept bills incorrectly on accounts with actual (non-estimated) meter reads, generating genuine billing errors that drive disputes. This is evidenced by disputed bills being dominated by ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025, E-02), a pattern that estimate-substitution mechanisms (AMI vendor gaps, field manual-read gaps, staffing shortfall) cannot explain since they act only through estimate substitution, and it is not a response-speed problem since ticket response times are within the 3.0-day SLA (E-04).

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route-log data (E-01) shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9200 manual-read accounts — a shortfall in the field manual-read collection step of the meter-to-cash process during the dispute surge period.

E-02 shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (total 3025); a clear majority of disputes occur on bills carrying an actual (not estimated) read. This limits how much any read-availability-gap theory (AMI vendor issues, field manual-read gaps, staffing) can explain, since those mechanisms act through estimate substitution and cannot account for the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population.

E-03 shows the billing-db tariff change log has zero entries, meaning no tariff/rate changes were made around the dispute surge period. This rules out a tariff-change explanation for the wrong-bill symptom, but it does not speak to the separate billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES/billing-config) that H-RULE-CHANGE actually concerns.

E-04 shows CRM dispute ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so slow response is not the operative problem for this ticket population regardless of the dispute surge.

release_summary.summary: SH-CS asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and "fix whatever is causing wrong bills" (CL-01), framing it as slow response. Ticket response times were already within SLA (E-04), contradicting that framing; dispute volume genuinely doubled from ~600/month to 1180 (Aug)/1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07). An initial diagnosis (PD-1@v1) blamed a rule change for miscomputing ACTUAL-read bills, based on disputes split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (E-02); this was invalidated by E-11, which showed the ESTIMATED subset is dominated by billing-import rejections (1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), coincident with rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-12) applied to AMI firmware v4.2 reading in 0.1 m3 units vs legacy whole-m3 units (E-13). The revised problem (PD-1@v2, DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS) explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset but leaves the cause of the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1785 of 3025) unidentified. The release delivered only the diagnostic, read-only scope: reviewing field route completion (DA-ROUTE) and monitoring dispute volume (DA-TICKET); it does not fix BV-17, correct bills, or determine the ACTUAL-read cause. Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, because open verification obligations and remediation items remain outside this release's scope, and fixing the rule or writing bill corrections requires Billing Operations authority (K-BILLWRITE) and change management not exercised here.

output.summary: SH-CS asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and "fix whatever is causing wrong bills" (CL-01), framing it as slow response. Ticket response times were already within SLA (E-04), contradicting that framing; dispute volume genuinely doubled from ~600/month to 1180 (Aug)/1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07). An initial diagnosis (PD-1@v1) blamed a rule change for miscomputing ACTUAL-read bills, based on disputes split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (E-02); this was invalidated by E-11, which showed the ESTIMATED subset is dominated by billing-import rejections (1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), coincident with rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-12) applied to AMI firmware v4.2 reading in 0.1 m3 units vs legacy whole-m3 units (E-13). The revised problem (PD-1@v2, DEFINE gate CONDITIONAL_PASS) explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset but leaves the cause of the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population (1785 of 3025) unidentified. The release delivered only the diagnostic, read-only scope: reviewing field route completion (DA-ROUTE) and monitoring dispute volume (DA-TICKET); it does not fix BV-17, correct bills, or determine the ACTUAL-read cause. Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, because open verification obligations and remediation items remain outside this release's scope, and fixing the rule or writing bill corrections requires Billing Operations authority (K-BILLWRITE) and change management not exercised here.
